problem: Strong specialist navigation/search executors still leave a task-level consistency gap: the planner's active stage, runtime evidence, memory and delegated executor can disagree, causing unsupported handoffs, stage lock, executor-context mismatch and over-scoped replanning. Prior feedback, memory and recovery methods treat runtime signals as generic context, use executor termination as a transition cue, or trigger broad replanning.
motivation: As local skills get stronger, the bottleneck in long-horizon embodied tasks shifts to keeping a coherent task frontier across planning, monitoring, memory and execution. Local executor status is not equal to global stage validity, so a typed, stage-level interface is needed to decide whether to continue, refine, transfer, promote or repair only a suffix.
key_idea: Represent stages as explicit contracts, convert runtime observations into evidence packets via an asynchronous monitor, and let the planner apply scoped updates (continue/refine/transfer/promote/repair) while pluggable specialist executors keep local closed-loop control.
insight: The paper argues that gains come from making task-frontier alignment explicit rather than from stronger executors. Its evidence is the within-type breakdown on the stress split: ContextFlow gets 62.5% handoff SR, 44.4% promotion SR and 28.6% repair SR where baselines get 0-12.5%, and on native R2R-CE early stops drop to 30% vs 53%/83%. There is no ablation of individual components, so attribution to each mechanism is only suggestive.
method: Stage contracts: each stage is <goal, handoff condition, expected evidence, compatible executor types, status>, generated online from the instruction and execution state as lightweight planner-side commitments

Memory: short-term subtask memory (observations, anchors, executor feedback, recovery events) plus long-term task memory (completed stages, key nodes, failure points, repair summaries); retrieved as context and validated against the contract and live evidence, never deciding transitions alone

Evidence packets: an asynchronous monitor aggregates observation, grounded anchors, progress cues, recovery/blockage, cross-stage discoveries, uncertainty and executor fitness into <o,a,p,r,d,u,q> and outputs alignment factors

Scoped updates: the planner maps contract plus evidence to continue, refine, transfer (change executor, keep stage), promote (advance the stale frontier) or repair (revise only the unsupported suffix, keep the validated prefix)
Delegated executors: AO-Planner for route-scale navigation, ApexNav for local search, AOPlanner-Low for endpoint approach; pluggable and responsible for local closed-loop control
Visible alignment board: an inspectable UI showing active contract, expected/live evidence, memory, executor, selected update and plan diff

setting.backbone: Local Qwen3.5-9B endpoint for planning/monitor; executors AO-Planner, ApexNav, AOPlanner-Low
setting.action_space: low-level continuous R2R-CE actions via executors, 500-step budget
setting.privileged: none stated for the method; the stress split rewrites instructions and diagnostic group labels are used only for offline analysis

numbers.eval_set_note: fixed 30-episode R2R-CE subset with native instructions (split not explicitly named in the paper)
numbers.extra: 500-step budget; budget-terminal pose evaluated; avg steps 343.07, wrong stop 20.00%, early stop 30.00%
numbers.evidence: Table native_r2r: Native R2R-CE results on a fixed 30-case subset

numbers.eval_set_note: 30 episodes with rewritten instructions (8 handoff, 9 promotion, 7 repair, 6 executor-context); source split not explicitly stated
numbers.extra: 500-step budget; rewritten instructions; Progress 39.61%; within-type SR handoff 62.50, promotion 44.44, repair 28.57, exec-ctx 16.67
numbers.evidence: Table complex_r2r: Mechanism-sensitive R2R-CE stress scene

numbers_note: Only two 30-episode custom subsets; the split of the official R2R-CE they are drawn from is not stated (val-unseen is assumed). No full-benchmark results and no component ablations.
results: On a 30-episode native R2R-CE subset ContextFlow reaches 40.00% SR / 24.65% SPL versus BUMBLE 16.67% / 5.48% and MoMa-LLM 3.33% / 0.58%. On the mechanism-sensitive stress subset it gets 40.00% SR vs 6.67% (BUMBLE) and 3.33% (MoMa-LLM), with much better within-type SR.
limitations: Very small evaluation (two 30-episode subsets), no official full-split numbers, no ablations of contracts/monitor/updates, and no comparison with standard VLN-CE methods

Stress split uses instructions rewritten by the authors to expose stage transitions, and is mainly a mechanism-oriented illustration; the baselines (BUMBLE, MoMa-LLM) were not designed for R2R-CE and use different executors
Depends on the quality of monitor outputs, memory retrieval and executor reports; executor-context failures remain (16.67% SR)
